input: Handlers must wear chemical-resistant gloves, protective eyewear, and long-sleeved clothing while mixing the pesticide.
Workers must wash their hands thoroughly with soap and water after handling the pesticide.
Individuals exposed to the pesticide must receive immediate medical attention if symptoms of poisoning occur.
The restricted-use pesticide may only be handled by trained personnel who have completed the required safety training.
Personnel must avoid eating, drinking, or smoking while handling the concentrated pesticide.
The container must display the approved product name, active ingredient, and registration number.
The label must state the permitted application rate and the crops on which the pesticide may be used.
The package must include the required hazard warnings and directions for safe handling.
The product label shall specify the approved waiting period between application and harvest.
All mandatory precautionary statements must appear prominently on the pesticide label.
A pesticide may not be sold commercially until the competent authority has granted the required registration.
The registrant must renew the product authorization before the existing registration expires.
Manufacturers must obtain approval from the regulatory authority before introducing a new pesticide formulation to the market.
The product registration must remain valid for the pesticide to continue being marketed.
A company intending to distribute the pesticide nationally must first obtain the applicable regulatory authorization.
Unused pesticide containers must be stored in a locked cabinet that is inaccessible to children.
Pesticide products must be kept in their original containers when not being used.
The pesticide must be stored in a dry, well-ventilated area away from direct sunlight.
Pesticide containers must be kept separate from food, beverages, animal feed, and medicines.
Partially used pesticide containers must remain securely closed while stored between applications.
The applicator must maintain the required setback distance from residential areas during spraying.
Operators must calibrate the application equipment before applying the pesticide to the crop.
The pesticide must be applied only at the authorized rate specified for the target crop.
Applicators must stop spraying when wind conditions exceed the permitted operating limit.
During treatment, the operator must maintain the required buffer zone around nearby ponds.
The pesticide must not be discharged into rivers, lakes, or other surface waters.
Use of the pesticide is prohibited where it could harm protected aquatic organisms.
The product must be used in a manner that prevents contamination of groundwater.
The pesticide must not be applied in conditions that could result in unacceptable harm to pollinating insects.
Measures must be taken to prevent pesticide residues from adversely affecting non-target wildlife.
The registrant must notify the regulatory authority of any confirmed incident involving significant pesticide exposure.
Manufacturers must submit an annual report containing the quantity of pesticide produced and distributed.
Any significant change in the product's composition must be reported to the competent authority.
The company must provide the regulator with monitoring data collected during the reporting period.
A suspected adverse environmental incident involving the pesticide must be reported to the designated authority.
